meta.description: Extract per-molecule embeddings from any encoder-bearing KERMT checkpoint (grover_base / cmim / hybrid / finetuned). Writes one .npy per readout type (atom_from_atom, bond_from_atom, atom_from_bond, bond_from_bond) plus canonical_smiles.npy and validity.npy. Calls task/extract_embeddings.py (which featurizes SMILES on the fly — no pre-computed features needed).

recommendations.title: Document metadata.pkl structure for downstream use
recommendations.problem: Step 7 mentions metadata.pkl contains canonical_smiles and valid plus 'other run metadata' but structure not fully specified
recommendations.root_cause: Focus on NPY outputs; pickle metadata treated as supplemental
recommendations.fix: Expand Step 7: 'metadata.pkl — pickle of dict with keys: canonical_smiles (list[str], RDKit-canonicalized per row), valid (list[bool], RDKit parse success per row), input_csv (str, source path), checkpoint_path (str), hidden_size (int), num_molecules (int). Load with: metadata = pickle.load(open("metadata.pkl", "rb"))'

recommendations.title: Add guidance for large dataset partial failures
recommendations.problem: No guidance on handling scenarios where some molecules fail featurization in large batches (thousands of molecules)
recommendations.root_cause: Assumes clean_csv validation catches all issues; on-the-fly featurization may encounter edge cases
recommendations.fix: Add to Common errors: 'Partial featurization failures → check validity.npy (or metadata.pkl valid key) for per-molecule success flags. Invalid molecules get zero-vector embeddings; filter these downstream via valid == True before analysis.'

recommendations.title: Add idempotency statement for repeated extractions
recommendations.problem: No explicit guidance on whether running extraction multiple times with same inputs produces identical embeddings
recommendations.fix: Add to Hard rules: 'Idempotency: embedding extraction is deterministic — same checkpoint and CSV produce identical embeddings across runs (bit-exact). Timestamped run directories prevent overwrites but outputs are reproducible via cmd_replay.'
